analysis:
This batch changes only the CI threat-review tooling. It does not touch provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or billing code covered by the threat model (TB-002, TB-011, A-001..A-017), so it raises no model-scoped regression.

Changes:
(1) .github/scripts/threat-model-review.py head lines 16-23 add runtime_seconds. THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS defaults to 900 and is bounded to 60-3000. Invalid values raise ReviewUnavailable. The alarm is now set inside the try at line 31, so a bad value reaches the generic handler at lines 38-41 and produces a non-clean 'Human review required' summary. This fails closed.
(2) bedrock.py head lines 46-57 and 66-84 add BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY, which accepts only fixed or workload.
- Workload mode sets a ceiling up to 500 calls (was 12, max 100) and 16384 output tokens by default. It uses a 600s read timeout (head ~133-134).
- The limit starts at 0 and grows only through plan_calls(count), which adds one repair slot. Exceeding the ceiling sets workload_stopped and raises BudgetStopped.
- The stopped property (line 88) includes workload_stopped, and the existing per-call limit check remains. Unplanned calls are therefore blocked, which fails closed.
(3) The workflow tests (lines 738-776) assert the following:
- pull_request_target is used, with the scanner checked out from the default branch.
- head.sha and head.ref are absent.
- timeout-minutes is 60, the workload policy is set, and workflow_dispatch and pr_number are absent from the review job.
- THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA no longer falls back to env.

Residual question, outside the threat model's scope and so not a finding:
- The default paid-call ceiling grows about 40x and runtime about 3x.
- pull_request_target may run for fork PRs. A large adversarial PR could drive planned calls toward 500 × 16k output tokens, limited only by MAX_SOURCE_BYTES and file-list budgets.
- The THREAT_REVIEW_ENABLED gating and who may trigger the workflow are not visible here.
- The plan_calls callers (budget_runner) were not supplied. Integration should check that the planned counts come from bounded source sizes, and that fallback calls to OpenRouter keep their own dollar caps.
